newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMI chief tries to keep time short for EMU choice.
newsitem.headline: EMI chief tries to keep time short for EMU choice.

text.p: European Monetary Institute President Alexandre Lamfalussy said on Tuesday all efforts would be made to shorten the period during which the final choice is made on which countries can launch the euro.

Lamfalussy acknowledged the risk of severe currency market turbulence in the March to April period next year when the EMI, the European Commission and European finance ministers debate the EMU start-group selection.
"I recognise that the likely one-month gap could be a difficult period to manage," he told a news conference to mark the launch of the European Central Bank forerunner's third annual report.
"The decision has been taken to try to shorten that period by as much as possible."
Lamfalussy said the EMI could begin working on its recommendation in mid-February next year and complete its report in mid-March, once final 1997 data are available.
Efforts would then be made to shorten the gap between the finance ministers' decision on the EMU choice and the parliamentary debate, he said.
A final decision, which includes recommendations by finance minister and the European Parliament, is expected in April or early May ahead of the planned euro launch in January 1999.
